original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Can standard-row completions and elementary input-basis shears reduce the P112 centre-output sensitivity while preserving exact co-delivery and rank-one augmented terms?
scope_change_reason: The previous bounded consumer audit established J=C^TUK but did not source Jx at the cut. Co-delivery puts the port update and centre correction on the same four tetrad terms, with native centre-frame orthogonal complements binding correction slots to omitted P112-root labels. Because the initial 92-entry matrix erases the local rank-mass saving under a one-unit-per-entry sensitivity, the package first exhausts the 70 standard-row complements on all blocks and then the 24 elementary integer input shears I +/- E_ij on every valid complement. This finite search tests whether the exact coefficient surface can beat the 112-copy local control. It is algebraic budget evidence only, not a physical supplier or proof of the global two-unpaid coverage contract.
bottleneck_link: The selected complex profile is binding. The full restricted complement/shear census preserves 56 rank-one terms but leaves minimum centre support 76, for a one-unit-per-entry local cost of 132 versus the 112-copy control. Further algebraic basis search has no task-level justification unless a source-bound scalar/endpoint contract changes the pricing model; the actual bottlenecks are an admitted native schedule and both supplier contracts.
stop_rule: The exact fourteen-block census of 56 standard-row complements and 24 elementary integer shears per complement is complete. Stop algebraic basis searches in this family: its minimum support-priced local cost is 132, above the 112-copy control, and the corresponding ideal complex ceiling is lower than the baseline. Reopen only if a source-bound scalar/endpoint contract changes the tariff. Do not begin construction without an executable dirty-input tetrad schedule, its frame/source/lifetime/restoration invoice, and a complete bit-side endpoint.
evidence: All fourteen exact block identities factor UK=(UE)E^T and J=C^TUK=(C^TUE)E^T. The selected word's native centre frames bind centre slots to omitted P112-root labels by [7,5,4,6,3,1,0,2], the unique minimum among all 8! assignments. Every one of the 56 augmented terms has binary support-pair rank one. Across fourteen blocks, standard-row complements lower C^T M support from 92 to 88. The exact census of 784 complements and 18,816 shears I +/- E_ij finds all 18,816 shears preserve four rank-one terms; the minimum centre-support vector is [2,7,7,2,7,6,6,7,7,7,2,7,7,2], total 76. Charging one rank-one unit per nonzero centre coefficient gives local cost 132 versus the original 112-copy control, profile {1:324,32:166}, local mass 5,636, and ideal two-unpaid complex kappa cap 0.0134440084459, below the 0.0137876681081 baseline cap. This is still above the requested 0.003 but does not establish a joint supplier or realized kappa. No physical scalar schedule, complete invoice, supplier admission, or selected-kappa update is established; selected kappa remains 0.001672660197076918.
